close_reason:
Replaced the existing .is_some_and(any()) assertion in chat_get_omits_ids_and_properties_when_none with assert_eq! on the full USING_CHAT array. Added matching assert_eq! to space_get_omits_ids_and_properties_when_none and message_get_threads_ids_and_omits_properties_when_none.

Coverage: 3 assertions total (one per method-family). All Chat/* / Space/* / Message/* requests in chat-client funnel through the same build_request(super::USING_CHAT) call site, so a regression that swapped USING_CHAT for USING_CHAT_PUSH (or vice versa) for any individual method in those families would fail the family's representative assertion.

USING_CORE / USING_CHAT_PUSH / USING_QUOTA are not yet covered because the methods that consume them (push_subscription_*, quota_*, blob_*, presence_status_*, read_position_*) have no smoke-test coverage at all — tracked at bd:JMAP-26di.6.

cargo test -p jmap-chat-client: all 94+ tests green. cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-client --tests -- -D warnings clean. cargo fmt clean. Committed as eadc01c.
description: Only chat_smoke_tests.rs::chat_get_omits_ids_and_properties_when_none (line 78-91) asserts on the `using` array of the JMAP request envelope. None of the space_* or message_* smoke tests verify `using`. The chat-client crate has multiple capability constants (USING_CHAT, USING_CHAT_PUSH per methods/mod.rs:195-208) — a regression that swapped them per-method (e.g. PushSubscription methods getting USING_CHAT instead of USING_CHAT_PUSH) would not be caught. RFC 8620 §3.3 requires using correctness on every request. Fix: add at least one `using` assertion per method-family that consumes a capability constant. The one existing assertion (chat_get) uses an awkward .is_some_and(|a| a.iter().any(...)) chain; replace with assert_eq! on the full expected array so 'extra capabilities accidentally added' is also caught.
title: using-capability correctness asserted on only 1 of 26 smoke tests
